newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on rumours of gov't buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on rumours of gov't buying.

text.p: The won fell against the dollar on Monday on rumours that the government planned to buy a large amount of the U.S. unit this week, traders said.
The dollar's strength against the Japanese yen on world markets also weighed on the local currency, they said.
The won ended at 834.00, down from the opening high of 832.00. It touched a low of 834.30.
"Rumours that the Office of Supply planned to buy around $200 million this week kept interbank dealers from selling dollars," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Some traders saw the won continuing its slide. "If the 835 level is broken we expect the dollar/won to go as far as 840," said a Societe Generale dealer.
But others said they expected 835 to be a strong ceiling.
The trading range for Tuesday was forecast to be around 832 to 835.
The Bank of Korea pegged Tuesday's base mid-rate at 833.30, against Monday's 831.
